buck.changes: neck 1.15x thicker about the neck line; darker forehead (#3b2c22); hooves and pasterns go with their leg part (the doe leaves them on the body, a doe fault left alone so the doe's output does not change); procedural mule-deer antlers built per tier and never decimated with the body: burr on the frontal bone in front of and inside the ear base, the beam up, out and back, an even fork at about 45% of its length, the rear branch forking again (mature 3x3), a small brow tine; tubes 2.5 to 0.5 cm, 6-sided on lod0, 3-sided with 1 cm minimum radius on lod1, one flat V per side on lod2; hard-antler colour burr #6b5843 to tip #d9ceb5
buck.antler_flags: _ANTLER: 0 off the antler, else 0.05 + 0.95 x the fraction of the way from burr to tip (growth, shedding, velvet thickening, colour); _TINE: 0 beam and main fork, 1 the rear branch's second fork (hide it for a forked-horn 2x2), 2 brow tine, 3 burr ring. extras.antler_burr holds the left burr centre (glTF axes; the right mirrors in x). Antler vertices are HEAD (6), weight 1, pivot Neck1.
buck.season: spring antlerless (collapse every antler vertex to its burr, keep tine 3 as the pedicel knob), April-August velvet (grey-brown, about 1.3x thicker about the burr, rounded tips), September-January hard, cast January-March (brief)
buck.accuracy_notes: Reads as an antlered black-tailed buck from the side, front and above: a forked rack sweeping out and back inside the ear spread, darker forehead, thicker neck. The rack is a construction from straight segments, so it reads geometric close up; the rut neck swell and stained hocks are not modelled; the body is the doe's scaled 5%. At a full graze dip (head flick 1.5 rad) the lowest antler point stays 0.78 m above the ground.

accuracy_notes: Source is a generic stylised deer. The build script fixes what reads wrong for a Sierra foothill black-tailed doe: ears enlarged 1.3x (mule and black-tailed deer have big ears), grey-brown coat with a darker forehead and nose bridge, small dark almond eye, tail black on top and at the tip and white beneath, a clean white rump patch. The buck is a variant (variants.buck, client/assets/deer_buck.glb). Open: the hooves and pasterns are skinned to the source's IK foot bones, which tools/build_deer.py does not map to a leg, so on the doe they stay on the body part and do not swing with the legs (the buck build fixes this); the bedded pose still looks sunk into the ground; the low-poly faceting is stylised rather than realistic. A local naturalist should check tail, rump and ear proportions against does seen in the foothills.
